history.dynasty: Panduvamshis (Somavanshis) of South Kosala - built by Queen Vasata, mother of Mahashivagupta Balarjuna (widow of King Harshagupta)
history.summary: One of India's finest early brick temples, at Sirpur (ancient Shripur), once the capital of South Kosala under the Sarabhapuriyas and Panduvamshis (6th-8th century CE). The east-facing red-brick temple stands on a high massive platform in panchayatana plan (garbhagriha, antarala, and a now-ruined stone-pillared mandapa); its exquisitely carved stone doorframe depicts Seshasayi Vishnu with his incarnations, and the sanctum shows Vishnu canopied by the multi-hooded Sheshanaga, with carvings of Krishna Leela and Vaishnava dvarapalas on the walls. Built ~650 CE by Queen Vasata - the mother of Mahashivagupta Balarjuna and widow of King Harshagupta - in her husband's memory (some sources phrase the relationship slightly differently), and dedicated to Vishnu; the 'Lakshman' name comes from a small black Lakshman statue found on a snake-hood inside. Reported by Alexander Cunningham in 1872 and excavated by the ASI, which maintains the site and an on-site museum (sculptures of the 5th-12th centuries across Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism). Entry fee CONFLICT (verify): Rs 25 (Indian) / Rs 300 (foreigner) per one 2026 travel guide vs Rs 20 per another source. CSV town 'Sirpur' is correct.

name: Lakshman Temple
town_description: Sirpur (ancient Shripur, 'city of auspiciousness') is a historic village on the banks of the Mahanadi in Mahasamund district, about 78 km from Raipur. It was the capital of South Kosala under the Sarabhapuriya and Panduvamshi kings (6th-8th century CE), and today its Hindu, Buddhist and Jain monuments - with ASI museums - make it one of Chhattisgarh's richest archaeological zones.

travel.road: On SH-9, ~35 km from Mahasamund and ~78 km from Raipur; all ancient sites are within walking distance in the village
